name: The Discourse
author: Frontier Lab Tycoon
description: FLT-33: nine factions with beliefs, grievances, chants and a grudge or two. Each faction is one entry in content.factions (add one, override one, remove one); its two events are the cards and the arc named after it. Meters appear at Level 4, protests and events at Level 5.

add.name: Accelerationists
add.blurb: Hoodies, countdown clocks and a firm belief that the curve is a personality. They love a launch cadence. They are a bit right and a lot loud.

grievances.text: You HELD a release. The timeline will remember this.
A bigger safety budget? In this economy?
You said the word 'concerns' in public.
You haven't shipped in weeks. Grandma is still doing her own taxes.
Every release now comes with a 90-page system card and a nap.

cheers.text: WE ARE SO BACK.
Shipped on a Friday. Legend behaviour.
More compute. The line goes up.
A whole datacenter. Beautiful. Brutal. Blinking.
Safety budget cut. The vibes are immaculate.

thoughts: The heat death of the universe won't prevent itself.
I put my savings in compute. Not a company. Just compute.
Sleep is a legacy dependency.
Every day we don't ship, a spreadsheet somewhere stays manual.
argue: The curve doesn't care about your feelings.
retorts: We'll fix it in the next version.

lines: That's what the last 40 incidents said.
Name one thing that could go wrong.

chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? THE FUTURE! WHEN? YESTERDAY!

fan: Accelerationists call {lab} 'the only lab still built different'
Hoodied crowd livestreams {lab} launch from a parking lot, calls it 'church'
angry: Accelerationists accuse {lab} of 'going soft', post 140-part thread with no chart axes
'{lab} got scared': Accelerationists unfollow in a coordinated wave
schism: Accelerationists and {other} split; each says the other 'never really believed in the curve'

add.name: Safetyists
add.blurb: They want evals, pauses and a system card for the system card. They read every page of yours, including the appendix you forgot to write.

grievances.text: You shipped the model before the evals finished loading.
A 'leaked' benchmark screenshot is not a safety case.
Another incident. They have started a spreadsheet of your incidents.
You cut the safety budget. They noticed before you did.
You put the weights on the internet. The internet is not an eval.
Three releases in a quarter and zero system cards.
Your safety team is one intern and a very tired dog.

cheers.text: A real safety budget. They printed it and framed it.
You held the release. They sent flowers (with a citation).
You said 'concerns' in public. Growth.
You published the evals. They are reading them in a circle.

thoughts: I read the system card. Then the appendix. Then I read it again, angrily.
Has anyone red-teamed the kombucha?
My p(bad) went up 2% at lunch. The sandwich was fine; the vibes weren't.
I'd like to pause. Not the model. Me. Just for a bit.
retorts: That's not a safety case, that's a vibe.

lines: We need a careful, measured pause.
We need a pause measured in *centuries*.
Evals are just the menu of the apocalypse.

chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? RED TEAMS! WHEN? BEFORE LAUNCH!
READ THE CARD! READ THE CARD!

fan: Safetyists praise {lab}'s evals; 'we only found 40 problems, a record'
{lab} safety report cited approvingly; footnotes described as 'lush'
angry: Safetyists publish open letter on {lab} release; footnote 212 is just 'why'
Safetyist reading group votes {lab} system card 'least readable of the year'
ally: Safetyists and {other} form coalition; first joint memo is 90 pages
schism: Safetyists and {other} split over whether 'pause' means pause

add.name: Doomers
add.blurb: A subset of the Safetyists, but with a timeline and a spreadsheet. Extremely polite about the end of the world. Bring snacks; they always do.

grievances.text: You shipped another model. They updated the spreadsheet.
Rushed launch. The timeline in their spreadsheet moved left.
Open weights: now everyone can end the world, democratically.
A datacenter. That's a very big spreadsheet cell.
You release faster than they can write obituaries for the old models.
You keep putting the dangerous stuff in a public folder.

cheers.text: You held a release. They cried. Politely.
More safety spend. The spreadsheet gets a new, greener tab.
Closed research. Fewer recipes in the wild.

thoughts: I updated my timeline. It's shorter. I updated my playlist too.
Enjoy the kombucha while it lasts. I mean that warmly.
My spreadsheet has a column called 'vibes (terminal)'.
I'm not saying we're doomed. I'm saying it on a sandwich board.
retorts: That's the most optimistic thing I've heard today, and it's bad.
Cool. Add it to the spreadsheet.
chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? MORE TIME! WHEN DO WE WANT IT? WHILE THERE STILL IS SOME!
HONK IF YOU'VE READ THE PAPER

fan: Doomers call {lab} 'the least worst', frame it
angry: Doomers hold candlelit vigil at {lab}; candles are LED 'for safety'
Doomer spreadsheet adds {lab} tab; tab is red
ally: Doomers and {other} agree the end is nigh, disagree on the font
schism: Doomers and {other} split over a pause letter's wording; both sides cite footnote 4

add.name: Ethicists
add.blurb: Bias, labour, consent and water. They have asked who labelled your data and they would like an answer, in writing, with receipts.

grievances.text: A gas plant next to the kombucha tap. Bold.
Another thirsty cluster. They have a water meter and a grudge.
A datacenter the size of a lake. It drinks like one, too.
You said nothing about the water. Silence is also a statement.
You lobbied for 'light-touch' rules. They felt the touch.
Your water bill has its own weather system.
Record revenue. Record who-labelled-the-data questions.

cheers.text: A Transparency Fountain. Symbolic, but they'll take it.
Solar! They brought a cake shaped like a panel.
Open research: at last, something to footnote.

thoughts: Who labelled the data? Did anyone ask the data?
I brought my own cup. The cup has a thesis.
Every prompt drinks a bottle of water. I have not checked. It feels true.
Consent is not a checkbox. It is two checkboxes.
retorts: Please cite a source that isn't a keynote.

lines: Other models. It's labels all the way down.

chants: HEY HEY, HO HO, ASK THE LABELLERS BEFORE YOU GO!

fan: Ethicists call {lab} 'less bad than expected', a career-high review
angry: Ethicists ask {lab} who labelled the data; {lab} replies 'a lot of people, probably'
Ethicist report on {lab} has 90 pages on water and one on the snacks
ally: Ethicists and {other} join forces against {lab}'s water bill
schism: Ethicists and {other} split; one side wanted a teach-in, the other a TikTok

add.name: Open-weights maximalists
add.blurb: Weights or it didn't happen. They will fine-tune your model to speak exclusively in pirate within the hour, and they mean it as a compliment.

grievances.text: Closed papers. They are drafting a very long post.
A new model and not a single weight. Not even a small one.
You lobbied for licences. They call it 'regulatory moat-building'.
Your weights are more locked down than the kombucha fridge.

cheers.text: Open weights! They're seeding it from a toaster.
Open publishing. They're already writing the fork.
A leak! Information wants to be free (and slightly blurry).

thoughts: Weights or it didn't happen.
I fine-tuned it to talk like a pirate. It's the best it's ever been.
Every closed model is just an open model that hasn't been leaked yet.
I run it locally. Locally is my laptop. My laptop is on fire.
argue: Open source is safety through sunlight.
Just put it on the internet.
retorts: Cool, we'll just fine-tune that out.

lines: Just put *you* online, see how that goes.

chants: OPEN IT UP! OPEN IT UP!
WHAT DO WE WANT? CHECKPOINTS! WHEN? NOW, IN FP16!

fan: Open-weights community crowns {lab} 'the people's lab'; fine-tune speaks only pirate
angry: Open-weights maximalists torrent a picture of {lab}'s weights 'as a statement'
'Weights or it didn't happen': Open-weights crowd says {model} didn't happen
ally: Open-weights crowd and {other} sign joint letter demanding 'more of everything'
schism: Open-weights crowd and {other} split over a licence file nobody read

add.name: VCs
add.blurb: Hype-positive and runway-agnostic. They would like to know about your moat, your TAM and whether you've considered agents for dog-walking.

grievances.text: You gave the weights away. Where is the moat now, hmm?
You held a release. Their LPs have questions.
A bigger safety budget is a smaller runway.
The revenue chart only goes up if you rotate it.

cheers.text: New model! They're already on a podcast about it.
Shipped early. 'This is what we invested in.'
Closed research. Now that's a moat.
Lobbying! Finally, a line item they understand.

thoughts: What's the moat? No, the real moat.
Have they considered agents, but for dog-walking?
I'm not here to invest. I'm here to invest.
Runway is a state of mind.
argue: Have you thought about monetising that?
Is this a feature or a company?
retorts: Love that for you. What's the TAM?
chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? RETURNS! WHEN? THIS FUND CYCLE!

fan: VCs call {lab} 'the next everything'; valuation rounded up to the nearest planet
VC podcast devotes three hours to {model}, two of them to the vest
angry: VCs quietly mark down {lab}; loudly mark down on a podcast
VC asks {lab} if it has considered pivoting to dog-walking agents
ally: VCs and {other} discover a shared love of 'velocity'
schism: VCs and {other} split after disagreeing about what 'returns' means

add.name: Policy wonks
add.blurb: Memos about memos. They are drafting a framework for your lab, and a second framework to regulate the first one. Surprisingly good at snacks.

grievances.text: An incident. They've scheduled a hearing about the hearing.
You lobbied them. They wrote a memo about being lobbied.
A leaked screenshot is not a disclosure regime.
You don't have a governance framework. You have a Slack channel.

cheers.text: You showed up to testify. With a binder. They're thrilled.
A safety budget! It has line items! They're weeping.
Open research gives them something to cite in a memo.

thoughts: I wrote a memo about this campus. Then a memo about the memo.
Is there a framework for the kombucha? There should be.
My binder has tabs. My tabs have tabs.
Light-touch regulation is my safe word.
retorts: That's out of scope for this working group.
chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? GUIDANCE! WHEN? AFTER A 90-DAY COMMENT PERIOD!

fan: Policy wonks praise {lab}'s governance: 'there is a binder'
angry: Policy wonks draft framework for {lab}; second framework to regulate the first
Wonks schedule hearing on {lab}; the agenda is 40 pages
ally: Policy wonks and {other} co-author a memo; memo about memo expected
schism: Policy wonks and {other} split over a comma in section 3

add.name: Pictogram Luddites
add.blurb: Vibes-based, loud and extremely online about being offline. They have asked whether the AI is drinking the water, in a 12-slide carousel, with a filter.

grievances.text: Another cluster. They posted a sad glacier about it.
A datacenter. Their carousel has a slide with a crying emoji planet.
Another model. 'Nobody asked for this' (posted from a phone).
You ignored the water. They made it everyone's lock screen.
Is the AI drinking the water? They're pretty sure it is.
Too many launches. Their feed is just your model now.

cheers.text: A fountain! Aesthetic! They filmed a get-ready-with-me in front of it.
You held a release. 'Brands learning to rest.'
Solar panels. Very on-grid-aesthetic.

thoughts: Posted from my phone: phones were a mistake.
Is the AI drinking the water? Asking for 900K followers.
I did a digital detox and documented all of it.
Linked in bio: my manifesto against links.
argue: Is the AI drinking the water?
retorts: Ok but the vibes are off.

lines: IS THE AI DRINKING THE WATER?

chants: LIKE AND SUBSCRIBE TO THE REVOLUTION!
signs: IS THE AI DRINKING THE WATER

fan: Pictogram Luddite calls {lab} 'one of the good ones' in a sponsored post filmed 'without technology'
angry: Pictogram Luddites post 12-slide carousel on {lab}; slide 7 is a sad glacier
'Is the AI drinking the water?': carousel about {lab} hits two million likes
ally: Pictogram Luddites and {other} team up; the collab reel has a 40-second intro
schism: Pictogram Luddites and {other} split publicly, in a story that disappears in 24 hours

add.name: Normies
add.blurb: The biggest faction by a mile. They don't know what a benchmark is and they don't want to. They just want the chatbot to write their wedding toast.

grievances.text: Their chatbot called grandma 'buddy'. Grandma is on TV now.
They don't know what a benchmark is, but they know a leak is bad.
They heard the robots are unsafe. From a robot. On a podcast.

cheers.text: The new one writes better birthday cards. That's all they need.
A fountain! Free water! Is it free? It's free.

thoughts: Can it write my wedding toast? That's the only benchmark.
I don't know what a 'model' is. I know it did my emails.
I asked it for a recipe and got a 14-step workflow.
Is this the cloud? It's smaller than I thought.
argue: Can it do my emails, though?
Which one is the good chatbot?
Is this going to take my job or do my job?
retorts: I don't know what that means but ok.
Sure. Can it write a wedding toast?
My nephew said the same thing, then he got a podcast.
chants: WHAT DO WE WANT? SIMPLE ANSWERS! WHEN? WHENEVER IS CONVENIENT!
signs: WHICH ONE IS THE GOOD ONE

fan: Normies love {model}: 'It wrote my wedding toast and I cried at my own wedding'
{model} tops family group chats nationwide; nobody knows what it's called
angry: Normies turn on {lab} after chatbot calls grandma 'buddy'
Poll: 61% of Normies unsure what {lab} does, 70% sure they don't like it
ally: Normies and {other} agree on one thing, can't remember what
schism: Normies drift away from {other}; say they 'just got busy'

add.title: The Accelerationists are throwing a 'vibe shift' party
add.body: On your lawn. There's a DJ, a countdown clock to 'the singularity (soft launch)' and a banner that says WE ARE SO BACK. Nobody has asked where the extension cords go. They go into your cluster.

choices.label: Host it
choices.hint: −$80K · hype +8 · Accelerationists love it · Safetyists and Doomers don't

effects.text: {lab} hosts 'vibe shift' party; the vibes shift twice before midnight
The countdown clock hit zero and they just started a new one.

choices.label: Send a cease-and-desist (in a fun font)

effects.text: {lab} cease-and-desist to party-goers goes viral for its font choice

choices.label: Livestream the GPUs to the dance floor

effects.text: {lab} livestreams its cluster to a dance party; fans blink along to the fans

add.title: '{lab} got scared': the Accelerationists unfollow
add.body: A 140-post thread says you've gone soft. It has a chart with no axes and a meme of your logo in a cardigan. Researchers are reading it at their desks, visibly.

effects.text: {lab} announces ship date; Accelerationists re-follow, change avatars back
{lab} replies with a 141-post thread; critics 'respect the length'
{lab} leadership logs off for a weekend; stock of nothing in particular rises

add.title: The Safetyists want you at their reading group
add.body: They'd like you to present your eval suite. Attendance is mandatory; snacks are not. The last lab to present is still answering questions, remotely, from a cabin.

effects.text: {lab} presents 400-slide eval deck; Safetyists ask for the appendix

choices.label: Send the intern who wrote the evals

effects.text: They sent the intern. The intern came back with a p(doom).
{lab} open-sources its evals; they are forked, then argued about, then forked again

add.title: An open letter (footnoted)
add.body: The Safetyists have published an open letter about your last release. It has 1,100 signatures and 3,400 footnotes. Footnote 212 is just the word 'why'.

effects.text: {lab} commissions independent audit; auditors ask for an independent audit of the audit
{lab} blog post 'We Hear You' criticised for hearing too little

add.title: The Pause Letter
add.body: The Doomers have drafted a letter demanding a six-month pause, and they want the Safetyists to co-sign. The Safetyists want 'pause' changed to 'thoughtfully decelerate'. Both sides want your signature by lunch.

effects.text: {lab} signs the Pause Letter; pauses for exactly one press cycle

choices.label: Offer a three-week pause (over the holidays)
choices.hint: Doomers +5 · Doomers and Safetyists fall out over it

effects.text: Doomers and Safetyists fall out over whether a holiday counts as a pause

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: Doomers −10 · they blame the Safetyists' wording

effects.text: {lab} declines Pause Letter; the letter's authors decline each other

add.title: A Doomer bake sale at your gate
add.body: 'While there's still time.' Every cupcake has a probability iced on top. The lemon bars are labelled 'fast takeoff'. They're very good.

effects.text: My cupcake says 12%. Is that good? It tastes good.
{lab} exec asks Doomers what the cupcake numbers mean; talk runs four hours
{lab} funds Doomer spreadsheet; spreadsheet gets a second tab, called 'hope?'

add.title: Who labelled the data?
add.body: The Ethicists have published a report asking who labelled your training data, how much they were paid, and whether anyone asked the data. The data has not commented.

effects.text: {lab} pays data labellers a bonus; labellers label it 'overdue'
{lab} says its data was 'ethically vibes-sourced'; Ethicists add a chapter

add.title: Panel invite: 'Is It Ever OK?'
add.body: The Ethicists want your CEO on a panel. The panel has seven chairs and one microphone. The moderator's first question is printed on the invitation, in bold: 'Why?'

effects.text: {lab} CEO survives 'Is It Ever OK?' panel; answer given was 'sometimes?'

choices.label: Ask them to rate you out of ten

effects.text: Ethicists rate {lab} 3/10; {lab} calls it 'a big improvement'

add.title: The Torrent Drop
add.body: Someone has seeded '{lab}_weights_FINAL_final2.zip'. It's 4GB of photos of weights (the gym kind). The Open-weights crowd says it's 'a statement'. The statement has 80,000 seeders.

effects.text: {lab} answers gym-weights torrent by releasing real weights; both torrents trend
{lab} releases its tokenizer 'as a treat'; community tokenizes the announcement
{lab} takedown notice torrented within minutes; has more seeders than the original

add.title: Community fine-tune jam
add.body: The Open-weights crowd fine-tuned your model to speak only in pirate. It is number one on the leaderboard for 'Arr'. It is also, somehow, better at maths.

choices.label: Put the pirate model on the homepage

effects.text: {lab} homepage now greets visitors with 'Ahoy'; conversion up 30%

add.title: The mega-round dinner
add.body: A table of VCs wants you at a dinner where the menu is priced in valuations. The appetiser is a term sheet. Dessert is 'a conversation about the moat'.

effects.text: {lab} closes bridge round over dessert; the dessert is also invested
VC dinner with {lab} ends early; dessert described as 'existential'

add.title: Your VCs suggest a pivot
add.body: Have you considered agents, but for dog-walking? The deck is 30 slides long. One slide is just a photo of a boat. Nobody explains the boat.

effects.text: {lab} ships a dog-walking agent 'as an experiment'; three dogs now have API keys
{lab} explains its mission to investors; investors explain the boat

add.title: A memo about a memo
add.body: The Policy wonks have summarised your memo and would like you to comment on their summary before they summarise your comments. There's a deadline. The deadline has a comment period.

effects.text: Policy wonks tour {lab}; bring clipboards, mostly for the snacks

add.title: A framework for a framework
add.body: The wonks are drafting a framework to regulate labs like yours, and a second framework to regulate the first. They'd love your input, or failing that, your absence.

choices.label: Send your best researchers to testify

effects.text: {lab} researchers testify on framework; hearing runs long, snacks run out
{lab} lobbies for 'light-touch' clause; clause turns out to be one word long

choices.label: Propose a framework for their framework

effects.text: {lab} proposes framework to regulate the framework that regulates frameworks; wonks delighted

add.title: A 12-slide carousel about your water
add.body: The Pictogram Luddites have explained that AI is drinking the water. Slide 7 is a stock photo of a sad glacier. It has two million likes and zero sources, which they call 'lived experience'.

effects.text: {lab}'s rebuttal carousel gets 12 likes, 11 of them from staff
Luddites tour {lab}, film the kombucha tap, caption it 'the water source'
Pictogram Luddites love {lab}'s gift filter; post it with the logo cropped out

add.title: A brand deal (filmed without technology)
add.body: A Pictogram Luddite with 900K followers wants to do a sponsored post calling your lab 'one of the good ones'. They'll film it 'without using any technology'. You have questions.

effects.text: Luddite sponsored post for {lab} filmed on 'a vibe'; somehow in 4K
They said 'with vibes'. I believe them.

add.title: Your model wrote a wedding toast
add.body: It made 300 people cry, including the caterers and the officiant. The Normies are calling it 'the only good thing the internet has ever done'. The groom has asked for a sequel.

choices.label: Put it in the ad campaign

effects.text: {lab} ad campaign features AI wedding toast; three more weddings booked 'just to see'

choices.label: Offer the model as best man

effects.text: {model} accepts best-man role; asks what a 'stag do' is, plans 14 of them

add.title: The chatbot called grandma 'buddy'
add.body: A grandmother asked your chatbot for a pie recipe. It called her 'buddy' and suggested a 14-step agentic workflow. Grandma is now on the evening news, holding the pie, which she made herself, out of spite.

effects.text: {lab} sends grandma a pie; grandma rates it 'fine, for a computer'
{lab} 'grandma mode' becomes its most-used feature within a day
{lab} blames grandma's prompt; grandma's prompt was 'pie please'
